summary: Right-handed overhead cast at the back stop: spinning rod stopped at the 1 o'clock position behind the shoulder, rod hand beside the ear, left hand on the butt, weight on the back foot.

roles.r_arm: rod hand on the reel seat

rules.why: rod stopped past vertical at about 1 o'clock (30 deg behind vertical)
the elbow drives the cast; hand beside the ear

text.action: an angler at the back stop of an overhead cast with a spinning rod
text.core: Standing with the left foot forward, knees soft; right hand gripping the reel seat beside the right ear at head height, elbow bent about 100 degrees; rod stopped behind the shoulder at the 1 o'clock position, its tip flexing back under the lure's weight; left hand holding the end of the butt in front of the chest; spinning reel hanging under the rod.
text.gaze: Eyes on the target spot on the water.
cues: stop firmly at 1 o'clock, no drift
reel the lure up to 8-15 cm from the tip before casting
the elbow drives the cast, not the shoulder
avoid: reel on top of a spinning rod
line not connected to the rod tip

sources.cite: Utah DWR / Missouri Dept. of Conservation casting guides: stop the back cast at 1 o'clock, release at 10 o'clock, follow through at the target (search extract)
Biomechanics of spinning casting 2025: the elbow has the largest range and angular velocity, the shoulder plays a small role (abstract extract)
